name: daylight-mini-rug

footage.look: Live-action documentary realism, shot on a full-frame cinema camera, natural skin and fabric, real dust and pollen in the light, subtle lens flare from the low sun, fine film grain, true-to-life colour. Late golden hour, the low sun raking across the clearing from the west, long warm shadows of the cabin and the trees across the golden grass, warm rim light on the treetops.
footage.physics: Physics: the rug is one continuous piece of cloth and moves only when pulled, feet stay on the ground until the rug leaves them, the phone and the can stay in the hands that hold them, nothing passes through anything, nothing floats, nothing changes size, there is exactly one rug, one phone and one can.

notes: Mini trailer 'the rug' (Colby's pick, 2026-09-08 evening, after the cabin chase, with his twist: the explorer steps off the rug and is the one who yanks it, and our man goes flying). One Seedance shot from a gpt-image-2 keyframe (board daylight-minis-keys, cell rug), 480p probe first, then 1080p; cut from the master with a draft narration.

render.prompt: Locked-off 35 mm wide, static camera, no push, no zoom, no pan, one single unbroken twelve-second take from this one camera only. Start exactly from the first frame and continue the same continuous take without any cut; the camera never changes position, height or angle. The clearing with the large red and gold rug flat on the grass, the young man in the lime-green bucket hat (soft, round-shouldered, heavy-set, washed-out grey hoodie, giant black headphones round his neck, baggy black cargo shorts, long white tube socks in black slides) standing on its left half with his head bowed over his phone and a matte black can with a green stripe in his other hand, and the explorer in the khaki safari jacket and pith helmet standing on its right half with his hands behind his back. For the first three seconds nothing happens but the young man scrolling and the explorer watching him. Then the explorer steps calmly off the rug to the right, bends, takes the rug's edge in both hands and yanks it toward himself with one hard pull, and the rug whips out from under the young man, who flips backwards off his feet and flies out of the frame at the left in one clean arc, phone and can and all. The explorer drops the rug in a heap, dusts his hands, straightens his jacket and strolls out of the frame at the right without a glance back, leaving the empty clearing and the crumpled rug. Sound: birdsong and a thumb on glass, a rug snapping taut, a yelp fading off to the left, a distant thump, birdsong again. Live-action documentary realism, shot on a full-frame cinema camera, natural skin and fabric, real dust and pollen in the light, subtle lens flare from the low sun, fine film grain, true-to-life colour. Late golden hour, the low sun raking across the clearing from the west, long warm shadows of the cabin and the trees across the golden grass, warm rim light on the treetops. Physics: the rug is one continuous piece of cloth and moves only when pulled, feet stay on the ground until the rug leaves them, the phone and the can stay in the hands that hold them, nothing passes through anything, nothing floats, nothing changes size, there is exactly one rug, one phone and one can. No text, no logos.
